axes.brief:
Competitive elections, parliamentary scrutiny and constitutional review constrain the Fifth Republic executive. Prime ministers need parliamentary confidence; the directly elected president has a strong independent mandate.
Focused six-question reassessment: The Fifth Republic distinguishes the directly elected president from the appointed prime minister. Parliamentary support can change the government without a presidential election; Article 11's shared initiative requires parliamentary involvement, and emergency lawmaking is constitutionally bounded.

Article 49.3 permits legislation without an affirmative ordinary vote unless censure succeeds; it does not permit ignoring a successful censure vote. No general citizen recall exists; shared-initiative referendums are tightly limited.
